name: Pac-Man
miniText: How should an agent balance collecting rewards with avoiding pursuit in a changing maze? NetLogo Pac-Man combines navigation, pellets, pursuing ghosts, temporary power effects, lives, and level progression. Pepels and colleagues [1] study real-time Monte Carlo planning in Ms Pac-Man, Gan and colleagues [2] develop another real-time search approach, and Bellemare and colleagues [3] frame arcade games as controlled evaluation environments. These publications motivate scientific questions about action selection and benchmarking; the NetLogo game does not thereby implement their planners. The concrete rules for ghost behavior, movement timing, power duration, scoring, and resetting define this baseline. Related arcade environments can differ materially, so scores are not interchangeable. The simulation illustrates an interactive decision process with competing short-term goals rather than a validated model of human strategy or evidence of general intelligence.
